Step 1: the white curved inverted 6x4 wedge brick (b4) is the hull of the swamp boat.

Step 2: the parts box says 2x black 1x6 plates. One is shown being lowered onto the hull and the other is already in place on the opposite side. Both are listed as resting on the hull b4, one along each side of the hull's studs.
I could not read exactly which studs of b4 each plate covers, so rests_on lists only b4.
Step 3 adds one white inverted double slope brick 4x2 (lego-4871). It is the only listed white piece of that shape.
It sits across the two black plates and the hull. The picture is small, so I am not certain which studs it covers. I listed b4, b5 and b6 as supports.
Step 4: two dark blue 1x4 tiles (b8, b9) go on the two sides of the rear of the boat, one on each side of the black plates' studs.
Step 5: the dark blue 4x4 wedge plate with 2x2 cutout (b10) goes on the bow, over the front hull studs and the front ends of the black plates.
The pictures are small, so the exact studs covered are my best reading. In particular, I assumed each tile also clutches the white slope b7 at the rear.
Step 6 adds one light bluish gray 2x2 45° slope brick (b11) behind the bow wedge plate.
I read it as sitting partly on the wedge plate b10 and partly on the black plates b5 and b6. The picture is small, so the exact studs covered are my best reading.
Step 7: the light bluish gray 2x4 brick (b12) goes behind the grey slope b11, over the black plates and rear white slope.
Step 8: two light bluish gray 1x2 clip plates (b13, b14) go on top of the 2x4 brick. One clip points sideways and the other points back. The POLICE slope (b15) goes on the blue bow wedge plate b10.
The pictures are small, so the studs each piece covers are my best reading.

Step 9 adds the black 3x2-2x2 bracket (space seat) on the rear studs of the grey 2x4 brick b12. It looks like it also covers the studs next to the clip plates, but I could not confirm that, so I listed only b12.
Step 10: two white 1x1 plates with vertical clip (b17, b18) go on the rear studs of the grey 2x4 brick b12.

Step 11: two trans-dark blue round light covers (b19, b20) clip onto them by their internal bar. The picture shows one being added, with the other already in place at the back, and the box says 2x. They rest on nothing, since they attach only by the clip.
I assume each cover pairs with one clip plate; the picture does not show which.
Step 12 adds the white 2x2 seat (b21) on the free studs of the grey 2x4 brick b12, in front of the black bracket, between the two light covers.

Step 13 adds the radio and the binoculars. I read the picture as the radio clipped onto the side clip plate (b14) and the binoculars onto the clip plate at the left rear (b13). I recorded the radio joins without a catalogue port, since the radio entry has no ports.
Step 14 adds the two yellow levers (b24, b25) on the front studs of the grey 2x4 brick b12.
The pictures are small, so which clip holds which item is my best reading.

Step 15 (the boat is turned over to show the back) adds the dark bluish gray 6x6 webbed dish (b26), the airboat fan. It attaches by its anti-studs to the studs on the back face of the black bracket b16, so it is a sideways stud join.
I recorded it as resting on b16, the only piece it touches.
Step 16: the white 2x2 plate with pin (b27) goes in the centre of the dish b26, with its pin sticking through to the other side.
Step 17: the black 3-blade propeller (b28) is pushed onto that pin and can spin.
The dish catalogue entry has no pin-hole port, so the plate-to-dish join is described in the method text. The propeller rests on nothing, since it only attaches by the pin.

No listed pieces are added. The page only shows the finished airboat with the park ranger minifigure sitting in the seat and holding the levers. The minifigure is not in the parts list, so nothing is recorded.
